predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: the Crown's Ireland outside the Pale, Dublin and the Protestant enclaves: after the 1641 rising the Confederates 'controlled two-thirds of Ireland, including Waterford and Wexford' by the end of 1642

successors.name: Commonwealth of England
successors.text: Ireland, 'annexed by the Commonwealth of England' after the Cromwellian conquest of 1649-1653

ledger.x: 1642: the Irish Catholic Confederation is formed at Kilkenny.
1642: the Pale and Dublin are fought over.
1643: the Cessation of Arms with the Royalists (15 September).
1649: Cromwell lands at Dublin (15 August) and the Cromwellian conquest begins.
1650: Kilkenny, the Confederate capital, falls in March.
1652: Galway, the last Confederate stronghold, falls in May.
1652: the Confederation ends with the Cromwellian conquest.

wars.name: Irish Confederate Wars
wars.outcome: English Parliamentarian victory: the Confederates held up to two-thirds of Ireland in 1642 and lost it to the Cromwellian conquest of 1649-1653; 'Ireland annexed by the Commonwealth of England'.

wars.name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory; Ireland merged into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland.

certainty.note: Held 'up to two-thirds of Ireland' with no treaty or survey line; the extent shifts with the sieges (Waterford 1650, Kilkenny March 1650, Limerick 1651, Galway May 1652).
